urls.title: Site urls or domains
urls.description: One site per line, a full url or a bare domain. Every site is read once: a line that repeats is free, and a line that is not a url comes back as its own free row with the reason.

maxSites.title: Max sites
maxSites.description: The list is cut here, and sites beyond the limit come back free with status NOT_CHECKED_LIMIT. 0 means the default of 100, and the summary reports the number actually applied.

onlyIf.title: Only sites using these technologies
onlyIf.description: A lead list filter: a site that does not use any of these names comes back free with status FILTERED_OUT. A name matches a part of the technology name, so 'shopify' finds Shopify and 'next' finds Next.js. Empty means every scanned site is delivered.

excludeIf.title: Skip sites using these technologies
excludeIf.description: The opposite filter: a site that uses any of these names comes back free with status FILTERED_OUT. Useful when WordPress shops are not your market.

timeoutSecs.title: Request timeout, seconds
timeoutSecs.description: A site that does not answer in this many seconds comes back free with status NOT_CHECKED_TIMEOUT. Raising it costs run time, not money.

includeEvidence.title: Include the evidence for every detection
includeEvidence.description: On, every technology carries the mark that matched it: a response header, a cookie, a script url, a meta tag or a snippet of the markup. Turn it off for a leaner dataset, the names stay.

userAgent.title: User agent
userAgent.description: An empty value sends a desktop Chrome user agent, which is what a site mostly serves to a visitor. Some sites answer a different stack to a bot, so a custom value is a way to look at that other answer.
